To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MBD is a frequent complication in kidney transplantation.
MBD is common and characterized in kidney transplant recipients by low turnover bone disease, often leading to fracture and loss of bone volume.
MBD following kidney transplantation is characterized by loss of mineralized bone tissue, often leading to osteoporosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to bone disease.
the development of new diagnostic and therapeutic tools for the management of MBD after kidney transplantation.
the study of the mechanisms involved in the regulation of mineral and bone metabolism in renal transplant recipients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single best approach for the management of MBD.
there is no evidence to recommend the use of any specific agent or regimen for prevention and/or treatment of MBD after kidney transplantation.
the best way to treat bone and mineral disorders in renal transplant recipients is to prevent them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MBD is an emerging issue in renal transplant patients, and that further research is needed to better understand and treat this condition.

there is a need for further studies to better understand the pathogenesis and clinical consequences of MBD and to establish effective preventive and therapeutic strategies in kidney transplant recipients.

MBD after kidney transplantation is a complex problem and should be approached by a multidisciplinary team of physicians, including nephrologists, transplant surgeons, transplant physicians, endocrinologists and rheumatologists.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bone health should not be overlooked during the care of transplant recipients.
MBD in kidney transplantation is a multifactorial process, and that a multidisciplinary approach is needed for the management of these patients.
the management of MBD should be tailored to the individual patient's needs, with the goal of reducing fracture risk and maintaining the quality of life.
